note: Permanent ledger of audit findings. Never delete an entry; mark CLOSED. Each CLOSED entry MUST have a mutation test in audit/mutation_tests.py that re-introduces the defect and proves a named test goes red.

defects.description: Config facts keyed by rule name only; a later region overwrote an earlier region's result (last-writer-wins), hiding a NON_COMPLIANT behind a COMPLIANT.
defects.root_cause: Insufficiently specific history key (rule, not rule+region+account).

defects.description: Under signing_required, an unresolvable source returned a soft finding BEFORE the signature-required check, so deleting source+signature bypassed the signing gate.
defects.root_cause: Ordering: soft-finding early return preceded the required-signer determination.
defects.mutation: MUT-F01: move source-None soft return before signer check ; expect RED

defects.description: Id-less automated entries counted by text (count gate) but were unbindable (binding gate skipped them); duplicate method_id inflated bound count; a keyed-but-empty series counted as bound.
defects.root_cause: Divergent identity between count and binding; list-based counting instead of distinct-id sets.
defects.mutation: MUT-F02: count id-less automated by text; expect RED

defects.description: Continuity check measured inter-point and trailing gaps but never the leading gap from the window start, so a series clustered near today passed a 6-month window.
defects.mutation: MUT-F06: drop leading-gap term; expect RED

defects.description: Facts stamped with the run date without checking observation time; a stale fact replayed on later runs manufactured fresh history.
defects.root_cause: Ingestion time conflated with observation time.
defects.mutation: MUT-F05: main() append_run require_fresh=False; expect RED

defects.description: load() turned invalid JSON into {}, so a corrupt existing history was treated as a first run and overwritten.
defects.root_cause: No distinction between absent (first run) and corrupt existing history.
defects.mutation: MUT-F07: load_history_safe returns ({}, None) on ValueError; expect RED

defects.description: Posture facts routed by service only, so an unrelated same-service check (IAM password_policy) scored an unrelated KSI (KSI-IAM-JIT), and all a service's checks collapsed into one posture metric.
defects.root_cause: Routing key was service, not (service, check); registry keys were bare service.
defects.mutation: MUT-F03: drop the check_filter reject (if False); expect RED

defects.description: A blanket except incremented the evaluated denominator on ANY API failure (AccessDenied, throttling), turning an unmeasured bucket into a negative (not-encrypted) outcome.
defects.root_cause: Could not distinguish 'no encryption configured' (a real negative) from 'could not read' (unmeasured).
defects.mutation: MUT-F08: count any error as evaluated; expect RED

defects.description: Inspector coverage read only the first page (maxResults=100) and emitted a binary ACTIVE scored 1/1, ignoring the nextToken so a 1-of-100 partial sample claimed full coverage.
defects.root_cause: Bounded sample reported as a complete result; nextToken (more resources) silently dropped.
defects.mutation: MUT-F09: ignore the nextToken partial flag (if False); expect RED

defects.description: Collection stamps datapoints in UTC while preflight used the host's local date.today(); at UTC midnight a current UTC observation could be judged future-dated, so the same code+fixture passed in CI (UTC) and failed on a machine west of UTC.
defects.root_cause: Two clocks: collection UTC, preflight local.
defects.regression_test: validation/scripts/test_utc_clock.py (asserts _utc_today() reads the UTC calendar day, not local)
defects.note: First MUT-F10 (pointing at test_mot_continuity) SURVIVED audit cycle N -- that test never calls _utc_today(). Added a dedicated behavioral test (test_utc_clock.py) that makes UTC and local dates diverge; verified it goes RED under the mutation. This is the mutation harness catching a real test blind spot.

defects.description: The submitted SDR's dailyData series, 30-day/1-year window summaries, and per-metric daily series used the host's LOCAL date.today() as the window ceiling, while the collectors stamp every datapoint in UTC (datetime.now(timezone.utc)). On a host west of UTC near midnight, a genuine current-day UTC observation is dated after the lagging local 'today' and is silently dropped from the submitted document -- a silent under-report of measured coverage that is invisible in UTC CI. Same two-clock class as F10, which only fixed sdr.py:_utc_today() (preflight) and never touched the SDR builder.
defects.root_cause: Two clocks: collection UTC, SDR-builder window ceiling local. Found in the whole-repo adversarial audit (not among the recent-change set F01-F10; build_sdr.py had no dedicated clock coverage).
defects.fix_commit: this audit -- import sdr._utc_today() and route all three build_sdr window ceilings through it
defects.regression_test: validation/scripts/test_build_sdr_utc_window.py (injects a divergent local/UTC clock; asserts a current-day UTC datapoint survives _derive_daily_data / _window_summaries / _derive_per_metric)
defects.mutation: MUT-F11: revert the _derive_daily_data ceiling to date.today() local; expect RED

defects.description: Concern that a process/document KSI's outcome method could read as a false claim that an AWS API assesses organizational-process effectiveness.
defects.root_cause: Not a correctness defect. Reviewed against source: the outcome rendering already states the honest boundary. mot_window returns note 'Coverage of the persistent-validation window, not a pass/fail verdict', and the 11 document/process KSIs already carry provider-deployed outcome-metric contracts rather than API-asserted status (shipped in 1.3.1). No wording overclaims machine assessment of process effectiveness.
defects.regression_test: n/a (labeling, not behavior); the coverage-not-determination invariant is exercised by test_mot_continuity.py and test_submission_readiness.py
defects.mutation: n/a -- no behavioral defect to re-introduce

defects.description: Concern that the scheduled collection/persistence path could imply an automated determination rather than durable coverage measurement.
defects.root_cause: Not a correctness defect. Reviewed against source: the persistence path is already labeled as coverage of the persistent-validation window (not a determination), and the durable per-KSI history restore in the CodeBuild path fails closed on any non-'missing' error so readiness is never evaluated against absent history. No wording claims the scheduled path produces a pass/fail verdict.
defects.regression_test: n/a (labeling, not behavior); persistence integrity is guarded by AUD-F05 and AUD-F07 regressions/mutations
defects.mutation: n/a -- no behavioral defect to re-introduce

defects.description: There was no single definition of release-ready. GitHub required only the `validate` status check on main, so a red audit-gate or security-scan did not block a merge; the AWS RELEASE_MODE build ran the mutation runner and oracle but not Bandit; `sdr.py release` ran neither. v1.4.0 (commit c7d43bd) was published while its audit-gate was red (MUT-F10 survived, 9 killed / 1 survived) and its release notes claimed 10 killed / 0 survived; the tag was unsigned although docs/versioning.md requires a signed tag, and no assets (manifest, attestation, SBOM) were attached.
defects.root_cause: Three executors each owned their own step list; the only enforced one was the weakest.
defects.fix_commit: this PR -- audit/release_gate.py holds the one step list (audit: oracle, runner self-test, runner, tree-clean; security: Bandit); CI jobs, RELEASE_MODE, and cmd_release all execute it; a `release-gate` aggregate job (needs all three, if: always()) is the single required status check on main; release.yml refuses unsigned or mismatched tags, re-runs the whole gate on the tagged commit, and attaches manifest + attestation + SBOM + bundle; cmd_release now instructs `git tag -s`. v1.4.0 is superseded, not moved.
defects.regression_test: automation/pipeline/test_release_gate.py (AUD-F12 block: definition completeness, CI aggregate wiring, RELEASE_MODE parity, cmd_release parity, signed-tag release workflow)
defects.mutation: MUT-F12: drop the mutation-runner step from release_gate.SECTIONS['audit']; expect RED

defects.description: A mutation whose target text was absent was reported SKIP, and skips did not fail the gate. A harmless refactor of a guarded line therefore silently disarmed the protection for a closed defect while the ledger still said mutation_verified: the gate failed open on refactoring.
defects.root_cause: SKIP was designed for a defect fixed on an unmerged branch and treated as benign; it is indistinguishable from a disarmed mutation.
defects.fix_commit: this PR -- any skipped mutation fails the gate; the two honest resolutions are retargeting the mutation or running on the branch that carries the fix
defects.regression_test: audit/test_mutation_runner.py::F13 (a mutation with an absent target makes run() exit non-zero)
defects.mutation: MUT-F13: `if skipped:` -> `if False:` in run(); expect RED

defects.description: Nothing checked that a CLOSED + mutation_verified ledger entry corresponded to an executed, killed runner mutation, so the ledger could claim a mutation the runner did not contain (this happened once before: a MUT-F02 was ledgered before it existed), and a runner mutation could exist with no ledger entry.
defects.root_cause: Ledger and runner were two hand-maintained lists with no reconciliation.
defects.fix_commit: this PR -- run() reconciles: every CLOSED + mutation_verified defect maps to exactly one runner entry whose outcome this run was 'killed', and every runner entry maps to such a defect; any disagreement fails the gate
defects.regression_test: audit/test_mutation_runner.py::F14 (missing runner entry, unledgered mutation, survived/skipped outcome, duplicate ids, and the real ledger vs real runner structural agreement)
defects.mutation: MUT-F14: reconcile_ledger returns [] before checking; expect RED
